newsitem.title: UK: Tories again press UK minister over BP shrs.
newsitem.headline: Tories again press UK minister over BP shrs.

text.p: Britain's main oppposition Conservative party on Thursday kept up pressure on Lord David Simon, Minister for Trade and Competitiveness in Europe, over his decision to retain a shareholding in British Petroleum Co Plc.

Simon used to be chairman of BP but Cabinet Secretary Sir Robin Butler has ruled he need not sell his shares in the oil giant, worth about two million pounds, because he will not be involved in any decisions affecting BP.
Gillian Shephard, shadow leader of the House of Commons, called on Thursday for an urgent debate on Simon's position -- a request brusquely rejected by Ann Taylor, the leader of the House.
"The minister concerned has followed questions of procedure for ministers, he is not involved in any breach of those and inquiries have been made to ensure that that is the case," Taylor said.
An aide to Tony Blair added that the prime minister was perfectly satisfied with the financial arrangements Simon had made and said there was no conflict of interest.
